findings.reason: the plan would need to name two sets — the ids the synthesis renders, used by carry-forward and the `replaced`/`carried` split, and the reserved ids the refusal adds plan section ids to — otherwise the node implements a real content loss under a misleading tag.
findings.text: §4 defines "the set of ids a synthesis can render" as the plan's section ids, `outcome`, its comment keys and the function's ledger run section keys, but `_render_document` emits a section only for `available = set(comments_by_section) | set(runs_by_section)` (reckon/evidence.py:353): a declared plan section with no comments and no runs is never rendered. The carry-forward rule then says an unmarked section is carried only "when its id is outside the renderable set", so on a legacy record an unmarked section anchored on such a plan section id is dropped and reported tagged `replaced` — which the plan defines as "an unmarked section a rendered one took the place of", when nothing rendered it; and the `carried`/`replaced` split no longer describes the loss it names. A worker implementing the rule as written produces that drop and a false tag; the refusal's reserved set may legitimately be wider than the render set, but the two must not be the same value.

findings.reason: either the done-when gains a case through the followup-add path, or `append_to_list` comes out of the deliverable; as written the plan asserts coverage it does not measure.
findings.text: §3's deliverable names four sites that must gain the refusal, including `append_to_list` (reckon/_store.py:2366), which is a live production path reached by the followup-add MCP operation (`append_to_list(project, slug, "followups", …)` at reckon/mcp_edit_plan.py:256), but the done-when's third case exercises only the `followups` append op and the `followups.<id>.body` set, and no negative control names the `append_to_list` path. A node can leave that site unguarded, pass all five cases and both controls, and still store deferred-work prose through the untouched path — which is precisely the hole the section exists to close.

findings.reason: adding the one sentence §2 and §4 already carry makes §3's gate receipts readable after the run; without it the node may satisfy its done-when with no durable log to open.
findings.text: §3 requires only that "the command's output and finding count over power_convertor's `docs/plans/` are recorded in the run directory"; unlike §2 (line 40) and §4 (line 53) it does not require that every log — the new test, the base-revision arm and ruff — sits under the run directory, starts with its revision and literal command, and ends in `EXIT=`. The base arm and the ruff arm are the two measurements a coordinator reads to judge the node, and unnamed they can be left in a scratch path or unrecoverable.

The refusal uses reserved; carry-forward tags an unmarked section on a reserved id this run does not render as retired, so replaced only names a section a rendered one took the place of.
§3's done-when now adds a case through the followup-add path that reaches append_to_list, with a control leaving that site unchecked.
